items.stem: State three precautions one should take while working with a machine.
items.answer: Three precautions while working on a machine are: (1) wash hands to remove oil and grease or use chalk powder for proper handling; (2) avoid wearing loose clothes, as they can get entangled with machines; and (3) concentrate on work and avoid talking. The chapter also advises switching off the electricity if the machine is not in use and avoiding touching the moving parts of any machine, which may tear-off the skin or cause a burn due to heat.
grounding: Wash hands to remove oil and grease or use chalk powder for proper handling.
Avoid wearing loose clothes. They can get entangled with machines.
Concentrate on work and avoid talking.
Switch off electricity if the machine is not in use.
Avoid touching the moving parts of any machine. This may tear-off the skin or cause burn due to heat.

items.stem: While opening a bottle containing liquid insecticide, the liquid fell on your clothes. How can you prevent its harmful effects on you?
items.answer: If pesticide is accidently sprayed on the clothes, they must be removed immediately. Any body part on which the liquid has fallen should immediately be washed with plenty of water and soap, and one should take a bath as soon as possible. The clothes themselves have to be washed thoroughly and must not be used again if they are not washed and dried, because they can cause serious insecticide poisoning.
grounding: If pesticide is accidently sprayed on your clothes, remove them immediately.
If accidently sprayed on your body parts, immediately wash with plenty of water and soap.
take a bath as soon as possible after the spray.
cover your body parts with a dress used for this purpose. Wash this thoroughly after every scheduled spray and do not use it if not washed and dried. It can cause serious insecticide poisoning.

items.stem: Electrical gadgets are used in all households. What are the requirements of these gadgets which will prevent you from getting an electric shock?
items.answer: The gadgets and fittings should be government approved (ISI mark), and MCBs (Miniature Circuit Breakers) should always be installed at the main switch board. Heated sockets and switches must be changed immediately if there is sparking, and the servicing of the electrical gadgets must be got done as per schedule. The accompanying instructions should always be read before using a gadget, no switch or gadget should be touched with moist hands, and one should always wear shoes or rubber slippers while using a gadget to prevent electric shock in accidental leaking of current.
grounding: Always use MCBs (Miniature Circuit Breakers) installed at main switch board.
Immediately change the heated sockets and switches if there is sparking.
Always read the accompanying instructions before using the gadget.
Do not touch any electric switch or gadget with moist hands.
Always wear shoes or rubber slippers while using a gadget to prevent electric shock in accidental leaking of current.
Always get the servicing of the electrical gadgets done as per schedule.
Use government approved (ISI mark), electrical gadgets and fittings.

items.stem: What do you understand by First Aid? What are the priorities you should keep in mind before administering first aid?
items.answer: First aid is the immediate and essential temporary care given to a wounded, injured or sick person, in an emergency situation, to reduce the suffering of the patient and prevent further complication of the injury or sickness before availing professional medical assistance. The priorities to remember before giving first aid are: (1) maintain ABC - clear the airway if it is blocked, check breathing and give artificial respiration if necessary, and give chest compressions if the heart has stopped; (2) check and stop bleeding by applying pressure; (3) immobilise broken bones; (4) cool the burns; (5) treat eye, nose and ear injuries; (6) tie simple bandages and dressings over wounds; and (7) transfer the patient to the nearest health centre.
grounding: First aid is the immediate and essential temporary care given to a wounded, injured or sick person, in an emergency situation to reduce the suffering of the patient, prevent further complication of injury or sickness before availing professional medical assistance.
Remember the following priorities before giving first aid
Maintain ABC
Airway: Clear the airway if blocked
Breathing: Check breathing and give artificial respiration if necessary.
Circulation: Give chest compressions if heart has stopped
Check and stop bleeding by applying pressure
Immobilise broken bones
Cool the burns
Treat eye, nose and ear injuries
Tie simple bandages and dressings over wounds
Transfer the patient to the nearest health centre

items.stem: What is CPR? When and how is it practised?
items.answer: CPR is Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation. It is a life saving measure used when the heart and breathing has stopped, that is, when the person is unconscious and not breathing. Starting CPR within three minutes of heart stoppage is very important or else the brain will be damaged. Circulation is maintained by chest compressions: draw a line between the two nipples and keep the heel of the hand over the centre of this line, place the other hand over it and give chest compressions pressing down the breast bone 1.5 to 2 inches. The airway is cleared by finger sweep if required and is kept open by tilting the head backwards and lifting the chin upwards, and breathing is artificially conducted by the mouth to mouth technique. The ratio of chest compressions to breathing should be 30:2, that is 30 chest compressions and 2 artificial breaths per minute, as a heart rate of approximately 100 beats per minute has to be provided. CPR is continued till either the person is revived or medical help arrives.
grounding: The person is unconscious and not breathing
Here CPR (Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation) is required. It is a life saving measure used when the heart and breathing has stopped.
Starting CPR within three minutes of heart stoppage is very important or else brain will be damaged.

Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR): Circulation is maintained by chest compressions. Draw a line between the two nipples and keep the heel of the hand over the centre of this line. Place the other hand over it and give chest compressions pressing down the breast bone 1.5 to 2 inches.
The ratio of chest compressions to breathing should be 30:2 (i.e. 30 chest compressions and 2 artificial breaths per minute) as we have to provide a heart rate of approximately 100 beats per minute.
The airway is cleared by finger sweep if required.
The airway is kept open by tilting the head backwards and lifting the chin upwards.
Breathing: Breathing is artificially conducted by mouth to mouth technique.
Continue CPR till either the person is revived or medical help arrives.

items.answer: Because self medication may be dangerous: medicines should be taken only if prescribed by a doctor. The recommended dose has to be taken at the prescribed interval and one should never adjust the dose oneself, since minimising or exceeding the dose and frequency of taking the medicine can cause undesirable effects. It is therefore important to take medicines only under medical supervision, and to always visit the doctor if one experiences any unusual symptom while taking the prescribed medicines.

items.stem: What do you understand by the term substance abuse?
items.answer: Substance abuse is the non-medical use of a substance, including drugs, that changes an individual's mental and physical status and affects the health adversely. Some substances that are not necessarily drugs work in the same way. Once a person starts using a substance his mental state is altered and the person cannot get out of this habit; the extreme dependency on the substance compels him to increase the intake every day, and this is called addiction.
grounding: drugs affect the body by changing the mental and physical status of a person.
Some other substances also work in the same way and are not necessarily drugs.
The non-medical use of a substance including drugs, that changes an individual's mental and physical status and affect the health adversely, is known as substance abuse.
Once a person starts using a substance, his mental state is altered and the person cannot get out of this habit.
The extreme dependency on the substance compels them to increase the intake every day. This is called addiction.

items.stem: List the long term effects of substance abuse. If your friend falls into the trap of substance use, what will you do to dissuade him?
items.answer: Long term effects: substances having a long-term impact lead to serious damage due to constant and excessive use; the effects show up over a course of time and are usually caused by progressive damage to different body organs. The health consequences include irregular eating habits, sleep disorders and poor hygiene resulting in poor health and low immunity, which predisposes the substance abuser to diseases and infections. Injectable drug users are more prone to HIV where the users do not sterilise needles and share needles to inject the drug. A user may even die suddenly from a so-called overdose, when one consumes more than what the body can tolerate, or from long-term damage to the organs of the body. Those who get addicted often lose interest in other activities, be it school, job or any other responsibility. To dissuade a friend I would make him aware of the implications of substance abuse and help him develop life skills, because peer pressure can be managed that way and one can also persuade the peers not to engage in unhealthy behaviours such as substance misuse. I would show him the ways of dealing with negative peer pressure - saying 'No' assertively, making an excuse, reversal of pressure, and giving reasons - and encourage him to get engaged in socially productive activities, which help to channelise their energy away from the menace of substance abuse.
grounding: Long-term effects: Substances having a long-term impact lead to serious damage due to constant and excessive use.
These effects show up over a course of time and are usually caused by progressive damage to different body organs.
Some of the health consequences include irregular eating habits, sleep disorders, poor hygiene resulting in poor health and low immunity.
This predisposes substance abuser to diseases and infections.
Injectable drug users, however, are more prone to HIV in conditions where the users do not sterilise needles and share needles to inject the drug.
Substance users may even die suddenly from a so-called overdose, when one consumes more than what the body can tolerate. Death may also occur from long-term damage to the organs of the body.
The persons who get addicted often lose interest in other activities be it school, job or any other responsibility.
Peer pressure can be managed by being aware of the implications of substance abuse and developing life skills.
One can not only save oneself from adopting risky behaviours under peer pressure but also persuade the peers not to engage in unhealthy behaviours such as substance misuse.
The different ways of dealing with negative peer pressure are saying 'No' assertively, making an excuse, reversal of pressure, and giving reasons.
Young children should be encouraged to get engaged in socially productive activities.
This will help them to channelise their energy, being away from the menace of substance abuse and also inculcate social responsibility
